title: The Half-Moon Hinge
skyStory: First quarter: the moon is lit down the middle like a cookie someone was too polite to finish. Still in Cancer, it is torn between staying in with blankets and going out to make something happen. This is the hinge of the month. Mars is jangling the car keys. Saturn has already packed a thermos and is waiting by the door, quietly ready for both.

reading: Half lit, half dark, and you'll feel both halves today. In the morning you'll want to build. In the afternoon you'll want to nap under a quilt. Both are correct. The trick is not to apologise to either one.

Somebody will push back on an idea of yours around 1 pm, gently but firmly. Instead of defending it like a castle, invite them inside and give them the tour. You'll find the weakest wall together and fix it in ten minutes. The [[Three of Pentacles]] is all about building with others, and you build best when you stop building alone.
joel.mission: Ask someone to poke holes in one of your ideas today, then thank them for each hole they find.
joel.omen: A door that won't quite latch. You're halfway between two things; that's okay, wedge it open.
joel.stoneWhy: solid ground for a hinge day

reading: The quarter moon asks one question: what are you willing to push for? For Nancy, the answer arrives before the question finishes. You know exactly which thing matters this month, and you've known since the snow melted.

Make one move on it today, a real one, not a planning move. Send the email. Book the call. Ask the question you've been rehearsing for a week. The Mountain is patient, but the Mountain also moves glaciers, and today a glacier gets a little nudge. Around 6, the shore will reward you with a sunset worth pulling over for.
nancy.mission: Do the one thing on your list that requires actual courage, and do it before your second cup of tea.
nancy.omen: Geese flying north in a ragged V. You're on course; the messy formation still gets there.
nancy.stoneWhy: a sharp edge for a decision

together.text: Halfway moon, halfway brave. Each of you name one small scary thing and do it by sundown. Report back with a single emoji of your choosing. If both are done, the cabin chimney and the shore both blink once tonight. Probably. Look closely.
